This is not your usual career advice to “find a great manager and the rest will follow”. That advice can actually be quite harmful for some talented and ambitious people. This is an advanced career strategy for experienced PMs and product leaders who want to make better decisions about which companies to join and which internal roles to take.

In this video:

Great managers are a lagging indicator of a company's success, so optimizing for them can lead you to turn down the best opportunities of your career
Reorgs happen constantly, which makes picking a company for one specific manager more risky than you think
Most major career inflections come from new responsibility, joining a rocket ship, or a role change. A transformational manager is the rarest driver of career inflections
Managers exist on a spectrum, from great to competent-but-overwhelmed to absentee to toxic. How much the manager should weigh in your decision depends on whether you're joining a new company or switching teams within your existing company
When the manager does matter, evaluate them on four things: whether they clear obstacles for you, whether you can delegate up to them, whether they recognize top talent, and whether they have the credibility to advocate for you
